To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the chemo- and the ergoreflexes contribute significantly to the regulation of the cardiovascular system and to the maintenance of the body's homeostasis; 2. they are highly interdependent and interact with other major cardiovascular regulatory mechanisms; 3. they change with age and disease; 4. their sensitivities are altered in chronic heart failure and in other diseases; 5. they can be measured by simple non-invasive techniques and can be applied in clinical practice.

(i) chemoreflexes and ergoreflex sensitivities can be calculated by using a non-invasive method, the phase-IV slope method, and (ii) the normal range data are 1.2–1.5 for the ergoreflex and 1.0–1.5 mmHg−1 for the chemoreflex, and (iii) the chemoreflexes are increased in chronic heart failure and in multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, and (iv)
the ergoreflex and the chemo- and the baroreflex are the major cardiovascular reflex arch that are involved in the adaptation to the needs of body.
